sources.title: Wyoming Constitution -- no personal income tax; Wyoming Dept of Workforce Services -- Unemployment Taxable Wage Base
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly. Wyoming has never had a personal income tax (one of 9 no-wage-tax states in this project). Quoted the DWS's own historical wage-base table: 2026 $33,800 (up from $32,400 in 2025, adjusted annually).

sources.title: Wyoming Dept of Workforce Services -- Unemployment Tax Rates
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched directly. Quoted: rates are 'assigned per W.S. 27-3 Article 5' -- a base rate (industry-average for new employers with under 3 years of experience, benefit-ratio-based for experienced employers) PLUS four additional rate factors summed together, mailed via an annual rate notice. No single flat headline figure exists in the primary source, the same NAICS/experience-driven shape already documented for Louisiana's new-employer rate elsewhere in this project. Cross-sourced range for new employers by industry: 2.28%-9.78% (secondary only, not independently confirmed against the actual per-industry base-rate table this pass).

sources.title: Wyoming paid family leave and local tax status
sources.verifiedBy: Search-synthesized (WebSearch, not independently fetched from a specific Wyoming statute this pass): no Wyoming city or county levies a local income/wage tax; no state-mandated or voluntary state-run paid family/medical leave program exists as of 2026. Workers rely on federal FMLA (unpaid) only.

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. No Wyoming city or county levies a local income/wage tax.
localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed; not independently verified against a specific municipal-authority statute this pass.

paidFamilyMedicalLeave.rule: NONE. No mandatory or voluntary state-run paid family/medical leave program of any kind found for Wyoming.

unemploymentInsurance.newEmployerRateNote: NOT a single flat figure -- W.S. 27-3 Article 5 assigns a base rate by industry (new employers) or benefit ratio (3+ years experience) PLUS four additional rate factors summed together. Cross-sourced practical new-employer range 2.28%-9.78% by industry; disclosed as cross-source only, since no primary single number exists to quote (same shape as Louisiana's own new-employer rate elsewhere in this project).
unemploymentInsurance.confidence: primary_source_confirmed for the wage base; new-employer rate mechanism confirmed primary, exact range cross-source only.
unemploymentInsurance.knownGap: Not modelled in the engine -- same structural note as every other state's employer SUTA in this project: experience-rated, an individual employer's actual rate depends on employer-specific history a static jurisdiction file can't hold. Unlike Alaska/PA/NJ, Wyoming has NO employee-paid UI component -- confirmed via DWS's own rate-mechanism description, which only ever refers to 'employer' contributions.

knownGaps: Local-tax and PFML absence are cross-source confirmed only, not independently verified against a specific Wyoming statute this pass.

Employer-side UC is documented (wage base primary-sourced, rate mechanism primary-sourced) but not modelled -- same per-employer-experience-rating gap as every other state's employer SUTA in this project.
The exact 2.28%-9.78% new-employer range by industry is cross-source only -- W.S. 27-3 Article 5's own per-industry base-rate table was not independently fetched this pass.
